definitions.name: energy_MAE_per_atom
definitions.value: MAE_E = (1/N_conf) * sum_i |E_pred,i - E_DFT,i| / n_atoms,i, in meV/atom (per-conformation per-atom absolute error, averaged over conformations). Total energies, not conformer-relative energies.
definitions.source_quote: Fig. 4a axis 'Energy (meV atom-1)'; text p.5: 'we compare the energies and forces on the molecules obtained from COMP6 benchmarks with respect to DFT'. matgl v1.3.0 src/matgl/utils/training.py line 495: e_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[0] / valid_num_atoms, valid_preds[0] / valid_num_atoms)
definitions.ambiguity_note: The paper never defines 'meV/atom'. Alternative: MAE of total energy divided by mean atom count; not used, because MatGL's own metric (behind Table 5 of the same paper) divides each structure's error by its own atom count. Also not the COMP6 README metric (kcal/mol total and relative energies, not per atom).

definitions.name: force_MAE
definitions.value: MAE_F = mean of |F_pred - F_DFT| over every Cartesian component of every atom of every conformation in the group, pooled, in eV/A.
definitions.source_quote: Fig. 4b axis 'Force (eV A-1)'. matgl v1.3.0 training.py line 496: f_mae = self.mae(valid_labels[1], valid_preds[1]) (torchmetrics MeanAbsoluteError over all components)
definitions.ambiguity_note: Not defined in the paper. Alternatives (norm of the per-atom error vector; per-conformation mean then averaged) not used. MatGL's logged test MAE is a batch-weighted mean of per-batch component MAEs, which differs slightly from the fully pooled value; pooled is the literal MAE over the dataset.

definitions.name: units_and_conversion
definitions.value: COMP6 'energies' are Hartree and 'forces' are Hartree/A; multiply both by ase.units.Hartree (27.211386024367243 eV in ASE >= 3.23). Coordinates in A. Accumulate MAE in float64.
definitions.source_quote: HDF5 'lot' = b'wb97x/6-31g*'; Methods: 'All energies and forces of conformers are calculated using DFT at wB97x/6-31G level'
definitions.ambiguity_note: The paper gives no conversion constant. CODATA variants change per-atom energies by <= 0.004 meV/atom, inside the energy tolerance. Max |F| in the files is 0.47 Ha/A (12.8 eV/A), consistent with Ha/A.

definitions.name: force_sign_rule
definitions.value: Model forces are -dE/dR. Before the batch, on 2 molecules (one ANI-MD drug, one GDB) compute Pearson r between model forces and COMP6 forces*Hartree; r > 0.9 keeps the stored sign, r < -0.9 flips it (record it); anything else stops the run for a report.
definitions.source_quote: Triage note: 'check unit and sign on a couple of molecules before the batch'
definitions.ambiguity_note: No sign convention in the paper. The rule uses only correlation, never agreement with the paper's MAE.

definitions.name: energy_reference
definitions.value: Compare the Potential's total energy output (model output * data_std + data_mean + sum of element_refs, as shipped in model.json) directly to the DFT total energy in eV. No per-dataset, per-molecule or per-element offset is fitted.
definitions.source_quote: Text p.5: 'compare the energies ... with respect to DFT'; model.json element_refs = [-16.518, -1036.373, -1488.652, -2046.008] eV for H, C, N, O (total-energy scale)
definitions.ambiguity_note: If the unit/sign check shows a constant offset, report it; do not remove it.

definitions.name: group_ANI-MD
definitions.value: COMP6v1/ANI-MD/ani_md_bench.h5, all 14 trajectories, 1791 conformations, 20 to 312 atoms.
definitions.source_quote: Text p.5: 'the ANI-MD dataset, which comprises molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories of 14 well-known drug molecules and 2 small proteins' ... 'whereas the molecules in the ANI-MD dataset have 312 atoms'
definitions.ambiguity_note: The file has 12 drug molecules + Chignolin (149 atoms) + Trp-cage 1L2Y (312 atoms) = 14 trajectories, not 14 + 2; only one molecule has 312 atoms. Whole file used; there is nothing else to add.

definitions.name: group_GDB_9-11
definitions.value: Primary (reading A, label = heavy-atom count 9 to 11): gdb11_09_test500.h5 + gdb11_10_test500.h5 + gdb11_11_test500.h5, pooled, 35670 conformations.
definitions.source_quote: Fig. 4 x-axis label 'GDB 9-11'; COMP6 folders are GDB07to09 (gdb11_07/08/09) and GDB10to13 (gdb11_10/11, gdb13_12/13); file names give the heavy-atom count (gdb11_s07 molecules have 7 heavy atoms)
definitions.ambiguity_note: The label matches no COMP6 folder. Reading B: 'GDB-11 source database' = gdb11_07..11 (59670 conf). Reading C: folder GDB07to09 (36000 conf). A was fixed as the most literal reading before any computation; under A, gdb11_07 and gdb11_08 (24000 conformations) are in no plotted group. Per-file MAEs let B and C be reported as pre-registered sensitivity only.

definitions.name: group_GDB_12-13
definitions.value: Primary (reading A): gdb13_12_test1000.h5 + gdb13_13_test1000.h5, pooled, 24000 conformations.
definitions.ambiguity_note: Same set under reading B. Reading C = folder GDB10to13 (gdb11_10, gdb11_11, gdb13_12, gdb13_13; 47670 conf), sensitivity only.

definitions.name: group_S66x8
definitions.value: COMP6v1/s66x8/s66x8_wb97x6-31gd.h5, 66 dimers x 8 separations, 528 conformations; forces present.
definitions.ambiguity_note: Energies are total dimer energies, not interaction energies, consistent with energy_reference.

definitions.name: pooling_within_group
definitions.value: For multi-file groups, concatenate all conformations and compute one MAE (energy: mean over conformations; force: mean over components). Not the mean of per-file MAEs.
definitions.source_quote: Fig. 4 shows one bar per group; no averaging rule is stated
definitions.ambiguity_note: Mean of per-file MAEs is the alternative; files in a group have similar sizes (11670 to 12000 conf), so the gap should be small. Per-file values to be reported too.

definitions.name: conformation_inclusion
definitions.value: Every conformation in the 11 files (101352 total; 0 NaN energies, 0 NaN forces, all have forces; elements C, H, N, O only). Nothing filtered. A conformation the model cannot evaluate is reported, not dropped silently.
definitions.source_quote: Text p.5: 'the molecules obtained from COMP6 benchmarks'

definitions.name: models_and_code
definitions.value: matgl 1.3.0 at tag v1.3.0 (a6ebaebd); weights pretrained_models/{M3GNet,TensorNet,SO3Net}-ANI-1x-Subset-PES loaded from the local checkout (state.pt git blobs 76ed498f, 270e5fad, 9cca3b06; model.json blobs a94bcbbf, 2b5e5392, 667a0689). definitions.source_quote: Fig. 4 caption: 'errors for M3GNet, transfer-learning M3GNet (M3GNet-TL) from ANI-1xnr, TensorNet and SO3Net with respect to DFT'; Methods: 'Due to the large size of the ANI-1x dataset, only a subset was used for demonstration purposes'
definitions.ambiguity_note: The paper does not say which matgl version produced Fig. 4. SI Tables S4-S6 list readout_type 'set2set' and TensorNet num_rbf 32, but the released model.json files use 'weighted_atom' and num_rbf 3; the released json goes with the weights and is used. M3GNet-TL out of scope (weights not released).

definitions.name: text_ANI-MD_values
definitions.value: The p.5 numbers are the ANI-MD bars of Fig. 4 quoted in prose; they are scored from the same ANI-MD computation. 'above 14 ... and 0.14' is a lower bound, scored for M3GNet only.

issues: The authors published no per-item or per-group numbers for COMP6 (no source data, no evaluation script in the repo); values come only from the Fig. 4 vector paths. No bootstrap tolerance is possible; tolerances come from the 3-dp plotting resolution plus a float32 and unit-conversion budget.

ANI-MD description vs file: the paper says '14 well-known drug molecules and 2 small proteins' and 'molecules ... have 312 atoms'; ani_md_bench.h5 holds 14 trajectories (12 drugs + Chignolin 149 atoms + Trp-cage 312 atoms), 1791 conformations, 20 to 312 atoms. Recorded as claims data-animd-ntraj and data-animd-natoms.

GDB label ambiguity: 'GDB 9-11' and 'GDB 12-13' match no COMP6 folder (GDB07to09, GDB10to13). Primary reading A (heavy atoms 9-11 and 12-13) was fixed before computation; under A, gdb11_07 and gdb11_08 (24000 conformations) fall in no plotted group. Readings B and C are for sensitivity only, from per-file MAEs.

The sentence 'This trend can be also found in other benchmark datasets' (M3GNet worst, SO3Net best) is contradicted by the paper's own figure: GDB 9-11 energy TensorNet 1.705 < SO3Net 3.889 < M3GNet 8.925; S66x8 force M3GNet 0.029 < TensorNet 0.045; Tripeptides force M3GNet 0.067 = TensorNet 0.067. Not scored (no number); flag in the report.
arXiv v1 says 'Table 4 shows the MAE of energies and forces' for COMP6; the journal version correctly says Figure 4.

The matgl version used for Fig. 4 is not stated. v1.3.0 still has the M3GNet three-body indexing bug (threebody_cutoff 4.0 < cutoff 5.0) fixed in PR #840; it is kept as paper-era code. A mismatch for M3GNet alone could come from this.
SI Tables S4-S6 (readout_type set2set, TensorNet num_rbf 32) disagree with the released ANI-1x model.json files (weighted_atom, num_rbf 3); the released files are used because they carry the weights.

The M3GNet-ANI-1x-Subset-PES README describes the training data as 'ANI-1x-Subset: 300K MD simulations and Materials Project ground state calculations' with a 991735/248355/248355 split, and the Table 5 caption says 0.9/0.05/0.05 while Methods says 0.2/0.05/0.05 per molecule. Out of scope (Table 5); noted only.

Energy tolerance 0.01 meV/atom and force tolerance 0.0006 eV/A are strict on purpose: same weights, same data and deterministic inference should land on the plotted 3-dp values. A miss beyond them is a real difference (code version, data handling, definitions) that the report should size in relative terms, not a reason to widen the tolerance afterwards.
